issues:
Verdict KNOWN upheld. I re-fetched all 5 confirmed citations myself and they check out:
- Tibshirani 2021: AM-GM named in Sec 2.1; eq 8-9 give k|c|^{2/k}.
- Hoff 2017: Crossref confirms CSDA 115:186-198.
- Kolb ICLR 2025: Thm 1 says 'same global and local minima'.
- Dai NeurIPS 2021: vol 34, pp 26884-26896; abstract covers l_p costs.
- Gunasekar NeurIPS 2018: vol 31, Thm 2a.

(1) Gunasekar anchor should be Lemmas 6-7 (arXiv v2 numbering). Lemma 7 gives min ||w||^2 = L||beta_hat||_{2/L}^{2/L}.
- This is an explicit l2 cost on Fourier coefficients, proved by AM-GM (App D eq 83).
- So the checker's 'implicit bias rather than explicit wd' understates it.

(2) Missed in-domain precedent: Morwani et al. 2024, already in refs.bib as morwani2024feature.
- Location: arXiv 2311.07568v2, App F.1, proof of Thm 7, eqs 7-9.
- It uses Plancherel on the l2 budget, then per-frequency QM-GM |u^||v^||w^| <= ((|u^|^2+|v^|^2+|w^|^2)/3)^{3/2}, then Cauchy-Schwarz over frequencies.
- Our app:models product-neuron budget (per-frequency AM-GM, t^{b/2} superadditivity, Parseval) is this argument generalised from (nu,b)=(3,3).
- It must be credited at app:models and at approach.tex.

(3) The step is also optimisation folklore. Poon-Peyre, Math Programming 2023, Sec 4.1: 'It is well known that quadratic variational forms exist for ... l_q'.
- Their Lemma 4 (mixed-exponent Hadamard form) and Prop 10 (3 factors) are more general than our equal-exponent step.

(4) Neyshabur-Tomioka-Srebro 2015 Thm 1: AM-GM plus homogeneous rescaling gives weight decay = l1 on the top layer. This is the per-neuron b=nu=2 case.

(5) The L_{2,b} exponent b/nu is the b=2 identity raised to the power b/2, since the per-neuron cost is (sum_t ||u_t||^2)^{b/2}. It is a trivial corollary and not a contribution.

(6) Live text problems:
- The checker's anchor, approach.tex:45, is now a commented-out '%Original' line (line 67). The citation sentence must go into the live paragraph at lines 52-54.
- That paragraph says 'minimum penalty (sum of the weights)'. It should be the sum of squared factor norms, raised to b/2.
- It says 'weights ... exactly equal'. Equality is in the factor norms/magnitudes, not the weights.
- 'A^{b/v}' is a typo for \nu.
- The constant is dropped: 'least penalty ... is A^{b/nu}' should read 'a constant multiple of'.

Search limits: WebSearch budget exhausted (200/200). All sources were fetched directly (arXiv, NeurIPS proceedings, Crossref).

extra_citations.why: Already in refs.bib, but not cited for this step. App. F.1, eqs. 7-9 (arXiv v2) runs the same argument for the quadratic network: Plancherel, then per-frequency QM-GM on the product of 3 Fourier magnitudes, then a sum over frequencies. app:models generalises this to (nu,b), so cite it there, e.g. 'generalising the single-neuron argument of \citet[App.~F.1]{morwani2024feature}'.

Optional optimisation-literature citation. Sec 4.1 calls quadratic variational forms of l_q 'well known'. Lemma 4 and Prop. 10 give Hadamard (multi-factor) variational forms of l_q quasi-norms, including mixed exponents, which contain the equal-exponent AM-GM step. Bib fields come from Crossref.
Thm 1: l2 weight decay on a two-layer ReLU net equals l1 on the top layer. The proof is AM-GM plus positive-homogeneous rescaling, i.e. the per-neuron AM-GM price at b=nu=2.
